newsitem.title: SPAIN: Basque lawmakers press compromise on ETA prisoners.
newsitem.headline: Basque lawmakers press compromise on ETA prisoners.

text.p: Basque parliamentarians tried in vain on Tuesday to resolve one of their major differences with Spain's central government -- the transfer of ETA guerrilla prisoners.
The government has been dispersing ETA prisoners throughout the country to weaken their cohesion while ETA itself demands they all be transferred to jails in their northern Basque country.

Four members of the Basque parliament's human rights commission met ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) prisoners' spokesman Juan Lorenzo Lasa at his jail in Madrid on Tuesday to press a compromise proposal.
But Spanish Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja rejected their request to follow up that initiative by meeting him.
Mayor Oreja has criticised Basque parties for not presenting a united front against an escalation of deadly attacks by ETA since the start of the year.

Conservative Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar's government rejects any blanket transfer of the 500-plus prisoners but, in a conciliatory gesture, has moved several ETA inmates closer to the Basque region since coming to power 10 months ago.
The Basque government has endorsed a compromise plan which was presented to Lasa, who himself has been sentenced to no fewer than 200 years in prison for several killings.
The plan proposes moving the prisoners to within 300 km (190 mile) of the Basque country. But both ETA's political wing Herri Batasuna and Madrid have rejected it.
The delegation had said it would also use the visit to Lasa to ask for the freedom of two hostages held by ETA, prison worker Jose Antonio Ortega Lara and Basque businessman Cosme Delclaux.
About 800 people have been killed in ETA's 29-year-old campaign for an independent Basque state.
